finding: The architecture is slot-permutation equivariant to float32 epsilon across every action table. Positional memorization is not the mechanism.
hypothesis: The scorer keys on slot position, so it can memorize 'the atom at slot 7 of this molecule' rather than transferable chemistry -- which would explain fitting training and failing held out for the atom-level families.
measurement_artifact: family_log_probabilities and action_log_z compared as nan because disabled families carry -inf by design (enabled = isfinite(action_log_z)) and -inf minus -inf is nan. Those should have been masked; it is not a finding.
method: Relabel the occupied slots of a validation molecule (same molecule, different slot order) and compare the SORTED per-table logits. Equivariance is structural, so no trained checkpoint is needed, and comparing sorted values avoids remapping teacher coordinates under the permutation.
open: The mechanism. No evidence-backed candidate remains. An untested orientation: the failing families select among many chemically similar sites within one molecule (219-420 marks over ~25 atoms) while the transferring ones select among coarser topological objects. A scorer that assigns near-identical embeddings to near-identical atoms could fit training by using the whole-molecule embedding to break ties, and that tie-breaking would not transfer -- but this has NOT been measured.
still_established: The transfer failure is real and family-specific (+2.86 to +4.55 nats on 72.8% of the draw, about zero for the other four) and is not explained by branching, coverage, capability-cell mix, or slot position.
